answer: In the PoA ledger each agent must submit a computational proof called a jade token that encodes a short, stochastic data‑generation task whose output is compared to every recent submission. The protocol hashes the result, maps it into a color‑space signature and rejects any entry whose violet component is within a defined distance of an existing entry, effectively discarding duplicate or near‑duplicate work. An attacker must therefore produce a tundra of unique hashes, costing linear resources per fake identity, which quickly exceeds realistic compute budgets.
